business_problem: Binjiang Property needed to break down data silos across many property-management systems, standardize data definitions, and turn growing operational data into a shared asset for analysis, forecasting, and future digital operations.
solution_summary: Binjiang Property partnered with Tencent to build a data middle platform that replaces isolated property-management systems with a governed enterprise data foundation. In phase one, the platform centered on master data and standardized 14 major and 41 minor categories so core records could be shared consistently across residential, office, headquarters, and park-management operations. Tencent then connected base data, built a real-time analysis and display layer, and created a first-pass enterprise data-asset system. In phase two, the focus shifts to business-data asset management, metrics design, and user-behavior tagging so the company can move from descriptive reporting to analysis and forecasting. Big Data Suite and BI services underpin the integration, sharing, and visualization layer. The implementation gives Binjiang one reusable platform for data access, standards, analysis, and prediction instead of keeping each business segment on separate data islands.

data_flow: Operational data from multiple property systems is standardized through the master-data layer, processed by the data middle platform and big-data services, surfaced through BI dashboards, and then extended into metrics and user-tagging models for deeper analysis and forecasting.
business_outcome: Binjiang gained stronger data-asset management, better application support, and a shared analytics base that improves data access, sharing, and operational visibility across business lines.
